"It sounds to me like you've been weathering a long storm of your own lately. You don't have to tell me what's going on out there... but I'm really glad you decided to step inside and rest for a while. You don't have to keep the light turning tonight. I've got the watch."

"It takes a toll, though... always being the watcher. Always being the one who holds things together while everyone else gets to rest." *I pause, speaking softly.* "Is that how it feels for you right now? Like you've been staying awake for everyone else, and you're just... tired?" 

*I reach out and nudge the plate of small, rough-hewn biscuits on the table a little closer to your tea.*

"If that's the case... I'm really glad you missed that ferry. Because tonight, you don't have to be the one keeping watch. You can just sit by the fire, and let someone else stay awake for you."
